summary: Added 13 new adversarial tests across 2 new files targeting 5 distinct Phase 4 regressions. All 13 pass against the current implementation. Each test was independently verified to catch the regression by reverting the defended line and observing the test fail, then restoring the line. The existing Phase 4 E2E (content-authoring-e2e.test.tsx) and the Phase 2/3 adversarial suites continue to pass. tsc --noEmit and eslint are clean. The repo's tests/measure_orchestrator_audit.sh guard passes (A11 satisfied: tests/*.sh contract suite present, A1/A8 supervisor checks clean, A12 peer-review rule for automation-supervisor.py in AGENTS.md). No Phase 4 implementation files were modified.

files_added.targets: Phase 4 thin composition seam (authoring-lifecycle.ts) deep-clone contract
Phase 2 handler hardening: approval-storage split, displayName fallback, inline-approval stale-hash defense, cross-org student visibility

regression_targets.description: authoring-lifecycle.ts reverts to shallow-copy ({...activity.props} or returning the props reference)
tests: mutating a NESTED field on the composer state after projection does NOT affect the returned payload
mutating a NESTED array on the composer state after projection does NOT affect the returned payload
mutating a NESTED field on the returned payload does NOT affect the composer state
mutating a NESTED array on the returned payload does NOT affect the composer state
repeated projections are independent — payload A mutating its nested props does not bleed into payload B
every nested props object across all activities is independent of the composer state

regression_simulation.passing_tests_under_regression: 2 string-leaf tests pass (string is a primitive so a shallow copy is sufficient; the array/object tests are the sharper probes)

regression_targets.description: reviewAuthoredLessonHandler wires ALL placements through component_approvals (or all through inline), breaking the split by kind
tests: the explore (activity-kind) placement records inline approval; the worked_example/guided_practice primary placements record component_approvals rows — exact split
the inline approval on the explore activity carries a hash matching computeComponentContentHash for the activity kind

regression_simulation.change: replaced the inline approval branch with a component_approvals insert for activity-kind placements
regression_simulation.actual_test_failures: 2 split/ inline-hash tests fail; 1 stale-hash defense test fails because there is no inline approval left to forge; 1 cross-org test fails because publish throws before assignment
regression_simulation.note: The Phase 4 E2E used approvalRows.length >= 2 which would NOT have caught this regression. The new tests pin the EXACT split.

regression_targets.description: normalizeLessonDraft regresses (or adapter regresses) such that activity.displayName is undefined at persistence time; v.string() schema column would reject in production
tests: every persisted activities row carries a non-empty displayName even when the adapter is bypassed (handler fallback path)
every persisted activities row carries a non-empty displayName via the normal adapter-supplied path

regression_simulation.change: removed `|| activity.componentKey` fallback in both saveTeacherDraftHandler and editRejectedDraftHandler

regression_targets.description: publishAuthoredLessonHandler drops the inline-approval hash check (forged inline approval hash or missing inline approval could publish a lesson whose explore activity content diverged from the approved version)
tests: publish is blocked when the inline approval hash on the explore (activity-kind) activity is forged to a stale value
publish is blocked when the inline approval is missing entirely (no approval object)

regression_simulation.change: simulated by patching the inline branch to insert into component_approvals instead
regression_simulation.note: The missing-approval test is a defense-in-depth probe; under R2 simulation it does not fire because the regression replaced the inline approval with a row, so the inline approval IS still absent and publish still throws. The test catches a separate regression where the handler forgets to check for the inline approval object.

regression_targets.description: getAuthoredLessonForStudentHandler drops the teacher.organizationId !== profile.organizationId check, leaking authored lessons across orgs
tests: a student enrolled in the assigned class BUT in a different org from the teacher gets null

regression_simulation.change: replaced the if (teacher.organizationId !== profile.organizationId) continue; with if (false && (...)) continue;
regression_simulation.note: Existing Phase 2 visibility tests happened to short-circuit on the missing enrollment row for the cross-org student. This adversarial test ACTIVELY enrolls the other-org student in the assigned class, forcing the org check to fire.

regression_targets.description: Try to publish after editing an approved activity WITHOUT the stale-hash defense — verify it throws
existing_coverage: content-authoring-drafts.test.ts:538 (rejects publish when an approved activity becomes stale after an edit — proves the edit handler drops status back to 'draft')
content-authoring-drafts.test.ts:1517 (publish is blocked when a stored approval hash for an example/practice placement is stale)
content-authoring-drafts.test.ts:1573 (publish blocked when one of several approvals is stale and the others are fresh)
regression_targets.added_coverage: The two tests under R4 above target the INLINE approval stale-hash path specifically, which the existing example-kind tests do not cover.
regression_targets.verdict: already covered; new tests add the INLINE path probe
